roi.title: Governance isn't a cost. It's budget you stop burning.
roi.subtitle: Adjust your project budget and see the savings range that requirements governance puts back in your pocket.
roi.methodology: Rework accounts for ~30% of a project's effort; 70% of that rework comes from requirements defects (≈21% of the budget). Ancoro cuts 30% to 50% of that share by catching conflicts, orphan requirements and circular dependencies before the build — recovering 6% to 12% of the budget. An estimated range, not a promise: actual gains depend on the project and method adoption.

features.title: Three points where projects usually stall
features.subtitle: Each module was designed from real problems in scope gathering.

items.title: Dual 5W2H (AS-IS / TO-BE)
items.description: Every requirement describes the current and future state, with owner, reason and date. It forces the comparison nobody does in a spreadsheet — killing the generic requirement before it costs dearly at build time.

items.title: Cross Matrix
items.description: Does one module depend on another? Does the integration affect billing? The matrix detects conflicts and circular dependencies while there's still time to act — not in the validation meeting.

items.title: Collaboration + Audit
items.description: Comments, status and field-level decision history in one place. 'Who approved this?' has an instant answer, no digging through a three-week-old email.

beforeAfter.title: Same question. Two realities.
beforeAfter.subtitle: The daily life of managing requirements in spreadsheets, Jira and email — versus having real governance.

rows.question: Who approved this requirement?
rows.after: It's in the auditable changelog, with author and date.

rows.question: What breaks if Contracts change?
rows.before: You find out in the validation meeting, when it already hurts.
rows.after: The Cross Matrix warns before it becomes a problem.

rows.question: Does TO-BE match AS-IS?
rows.before: Nobody checks. The spreadsheet only shows the future.

rows.question: Does this requirement serve any objective?
rows.before: Orphan requirements slip by until go-live.
rows.after: Requirements without an objective are flagged automatically.
